To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
corrective responses in upper-limb motor tasks are directed toward the unpertubed trajectory when a desired trajectory is the goal.
the motor system can return the limb to the original trajectory, but only when a desired trajectory is the goal.

the human motor cortex can generate corrective responses to maintain the limb on a specified trajectory when the trajectory is the goal, but that these responses disappear when the trajectory is not a behavioral goal of the task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the neural processes that control the timing and direction of movement corrections.
how the human motor system plans and controls movement, and how these control processes are influenced by the behavioral goal of a task.
how the brain computes and executes motor actions, and we have shown that the motor system can be a trajectory controller but this depends on the behavioral goal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
trajectory control is an emergent property of the motor system when a desired trajectory is the goal.

trajectory control is a goal of the motor system, and that the goal can be to return the limb to an original trajectory, to reach a spatial goal, or to intercept a moving target, but that these goals can only be achieved if they are made an explicit part of the task.
trajectory control is not an invariant property of the motor system but is dependent on the behavioral context of the motor task and the behavioral goal of that task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the motor system behaves like a trajectory controller only if it is the goal of a motor task.

the motor system has the flexibility to behave as an optimal controller when reaching to a static spatial goal, or as a trajectory controller when reaching to an imposed trajectory or tracking a moving goal.
trajectory control is a behavioral strategy that can be implemented by the human motor system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the motor control system is flexible and context dependent.
motor control can be understood by examining the behavioral goal of a motor task, not by assuming the motor system is always implementing a desired trajectory.
the motor cortex does not compute a “desired trajectory,” but can behave like a controller that computes a trajectory when that trajectory is the explicit goal of the movement task.
